graph_requirements: Exp output reaches a Mul through only static element-order-preserving views
the Mul scale is immutable floating, finite, strictly positive, and provably broadcastable
the pre-Exp insertion or bias-combination point preserves element correspondence

observation: A broadcast positive scale remained as a full-tensor Mul after Exp.
mechanism: For finite strictly positive C, Exp(z)*C equals Exp(z+log(C)); combining log(C) with an existing bias removes the full-tensor Mul without adding runtime work.

expected_evidence.graph: Eligible post-Exp Mul disappears and output identity is preserved
expected_evidence.trace: The corresponding QNN Mul disappears without new Transpose or partition

outcome.performance: Correctness-valid paired target-device evidence confirmed an incremental gain for a matching graph.
outcome.mechanism: Matched provider trace removed the expected multiply without new layout or partition work.
outcome.quality: Tensor correctness and performance were tested; floating-point reordering still requires task-appropriate quality acceptance for each matching run.

safety: task-appropriate quality validation when outputs are user-visible
counterexamples: Zero, negative, non-finite, dynamic, or ambiguously broadcast scales are ineligible.
The floating-point operation order changes, so algebra alone is not a quality verdict.

provenance.scope_note: exact model, graph occurrence, toolchain, artifacts, and measurements remain run-local

discovery.lesson: A finite positive post-Exp scale can move into the log domain with explicit quality validation.
